q83.text:
The graph shows how the speed of an object varies with time.

[A speed–time graph: at time P the graph is horizontal at a non-zero speed; it then slopes down to zero, stays at zero, then slopes steeply upward passing time Q, before levelling off horizontally.]

A at rest | accelerating
B at rest | decelerating
C moving with constant speed | accelerating
D moving with constant speed | decelerating

q84.text:
A concrete block falls vertically from an aeroplane.

The concrete block falls into the sea and sinks.

Which graph shows the vertical motion of the concrete block?
[Four speed–time graphs labelled A, B, C, D. All start at (0, 0). In A, speed increases with an increasing gradient, then drops to zero and rises to a constant value. In B, speed increases with an increasing gradient, then rapidly decreases to a lower non-zero constant value. In C, speed increases with a decreasing gradient, then rapidly decreases to a lower non-zero constant value. In D, speed increases with a decreasing gradient, then drops to zero and rises to a constant value.]

q85.text:
Object P moves at a constant speed of 5 m/s repeatedly backwards and forwards in a straight line.

Object Q moves at a constant speed of 5 m/s vertically downwards.

Object R moves at a constant speed of 5 m/s in a circle.

Which objects are moving with uniform velocity?
A P only
B Q only
C R only
D Q and R

q86.text:
The diagram shows a velocity–time graph for an object which is accelerating.
[Velocity–time graph with velocity on the y-axis ranging from 0 to 120 m/s and time on the x-axis from 0 to 40 s. A straight line starts at (0, 20) and ends at (40, 120).]
What is the acceleration of the object?
A 0.40 m/s^2
B 2.5 m/s^2
C 3.0 m/s^2
D 100 m/s^2

q87.text:
An object is moving with uniform deceleration.

Which statement describes its motion?
A Its rate of change of speed is decreasing.
B Its speed is constant.
C Its speed is decreasing.
D Its speed is increasing.

q88.text:
The graph shows how the speed of a car varies during part of its journey.
[Speed–time graph showing speed in m/s from 0 to 20 against time in s from 0 to 12. From 0 s to 6 s, speed is horizontal at 10 m/s. From 6 s to 10 s, speed increases linearly from 10 m/s to 15 m/s.]
What is the value of the car’s acceleration between 6 s and 10 s?
A 0.50 m/s^2
B 0.80 m/s^2
C 1.25 m/s^2
D 1.50 m/s^2

q89.text:
The gravitational field strength on the Moon is less than on the Earth.

Which of these is different when done on the Moon compared with when done on the Earth?
A the gravitational potential energy gained by a stone lifted through the same vertical height
B the kinetic energy gained by a ball when hit with the same force for the same period of time
C the momentum gained by a bullet when fired from the same gun
D the work done in accelerating a stone from rest to the same speed

q90.text:
The velocity of an object increases from 30 m/s to 50 m/s in 5.0 seconds.

What is the average acceleration of the object?
A 0.10 m/s^2
B 0.25 m/s^2
C 4.0 m/s^2
D 10 m/s^2

q91.text:
A heavy metal ball falls vertically downwards through air past four equally spaced levels J, K, L and M.
[Diagram showing a metal ball falling vertically past four equally spaced horizontal dashed lines labelled level J, level K, level L, level M.]
The times taken to fall from one level to the next are measured.
Where is the speed of the ball greatest and which time is shortest?
A speed is greatest between J and K ; time is shortest between J and K
B speed is greatest between J and K ; time is shortest between L and M
C speed is greatest between L and M ; time is shortest between J and K
D speed is greatest between L and M ; time is shortest between L and M

q92.text:
Four objects are moving along a straight line.

The distance of an object from a fixed point on the line is plotted against time for each object.

Which object is decelerating?

A [distance from fixed point against time graph showing a straight line with a constant positive gradient passing through the origin]
B [distance from fixed point against time graph showing a curve starting at the origin with an increasing gradient]
C [distance from fixed point against time graph showing a curve starting at the origin with a decreasing gradient]
D [distance from fixed point against time graph showing a straight line with a constant negative gradient]

q93.text:
A brass ball and a feather are released at the same time.

On Earth, the ball reaches the ground first.

On the Moon, they reach the ground at the same time.

What is the explanation for this?

A Both weigh the same on the Moon.
B Both weigh less on the Moon.
C There is a greater air resistance on the Moon.
D There is no air resistance on the Moon.

q94.text:
A light object is dropped from rest. It falls a large distance vertically through air.

How can the motion of the object be described?

A constant acceleration
B increasing acceleration
C decreasing acceleration and then moving at terminal velocity
D increasing acceleration and then moving at terminal velocity

q95.text:
A car travels at an average speed of 60 km/h for 15 minutes.

How far does the car travel in 15 minutes?

B 15 km
C 240 km
D 900 km

q96.text:
The graph shows how the speed of a car varies during part of a journey.

A A
B B
C C

A parachutist is falling through the air at terminal velocity.

B Every force acting on the parachutist is equal to zero and his velocity is equal to zero.
C The resultant force acting on the parachutist is equal to zero and his acceleration is equal to zero.
D The resultant force acting on the parachutist is equal to zero and his velocity is equal to zero.

[A speed-time graph shows a curve of increasing gradient passing through (4.0 s, 9.0 m/s). A dashed tangent line is drawn at t = 4.0 s, forming a gradient triangle between (2.0 s, 3.0 m/s) and (5.0 s, 12.0 m/s).]

B 0.44 m/s^2

A A
B B
C C
D D

When does an object falling vertically through the air reach terminal velocity?

B when the acceleration of the object is equal to g

A car is moving along a straight, level road, with a constant acceleration.

B [Graph of distance against time showing a straight line through the origin with positive gradient]
C [Graph of speed against time showing a horizontal line above zero]
D [Graph of speed against time showing a straight line through the origin with positive gradient]

A A
B B
C C
D D

B [Graph of speed against time: steep straight increase then shallow linear decrease]

A
B
C
D

A
B
C

A
B
C

A It decreases because of air resistance.
B It decreases because of gravity.

The gravitational field strength on the Earth is greater than the gravitational field strength on the Moon. The Earth has an atmosphere, but the Moon does not.

B 2500 kg
C 77 000 kg
D 2 500 000 kg

B 3.0 kg
C 5.0 kg
D 18 kg

B Mass is a force.
